observation_summary: The compiler crashes with a NullPointerException when processing an interface that extends multiple non-existent interfaces.
reasoning_summary: The crash occurs at line 1574 in TypeCheck.java because implicitProto is null when calling getOwnPropertyNames(). The code assumes that the interfaceType always has a valid implicit prototype, but this assumption fails when the interface is invalid (e.g., non-existent). A null check on implicitProto is missing to handle this invalid state gracefully.
evidence_used: TypeCheck.java:1572-1573: // This can be the case if interfaceType is proxy to a non-existent object (which is a bad type annotation, but shouldn't crash).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a flaw in the algorithm's logic itself, but a missing guard against an invalid input state (null object) that causes the algorithm to crash.
This is a local procedural error in handling a specific edge case, not a missing design-level capability.
